advances: Two explicit witnesses for the stated boxes. The forced-chain bound applies to every compatible box-center vector. The zero-section bound gives a distinct witness and constant for the proportional shifts.

proof:
The four base points $(0,-2,0),(0,-1,0),(0,0,0),(0,1,0)$ are consecutive and collinear. They are all the sampled sites on that segment, so they form a closed minor. Their widths form an arithmetic progression of difference $-143/14560$. The compatible-center lemma on the midpoint relations at indices $2$ and $3$ forces $2c_2=c_1+c_3$ and $2c_3=c_2+c_4$. Their actual lifted centroids therefore lie on one line in the displayed order. Through the centroid at index $2$, any closed ambient halfspace contains either the left pair of centroids, the right triple, or all four when its normal is constant on the line. An arbitrary containing halfspace contains the parallel through-centroid one. Central symmetry gives at least half the volume from each box whose centroid is captured, regardless of the trace direction, including whole-fiber traces. The fibers are disjoint. Thus the depth is at least $\tfrac12\min(w_1+w_2,w_2+w_3+w_4)=443/5824$. The four widths sum to $1929/7280$. The binomial bound $(1+1/d)^d\ge2$ gives $\Gamma_d\le1/2$ and the strict surplus.

For $c_p=\varepsilon w_p$, $0$ is interior to every box. For any through-zero continuous halfspace, normalize the fiber volume to a probability and project on its normal $u$. If $u_1=0$, the projected law is symmetric and each closed side through zero has probability at least $1/2$. If $u_1\ne0$, the projected variable is $U+Z+\varepsilon u_1w_p$, with $U$ uniform on a centered interval of length $|u_1|w_p$ and $Z$ independent and symmetric. The density of $U+Z$ is at most $1/(|u_1|w_p)$, by conditioning on $Z$. It is symmetric and nonatomic, so changing its threshold by at most $\varepsilon |u_1|w_p$ decreases the half mass by at most $\varepsilon$. Moving a containing halfspace away from zero only increases its captured mass. The adverse first-axis halfspace attains the lower bound, proving the exact ordinary depth for every $d\ge1$.

Apply f4547c4166b39683 to the complete $P$, labeled by its seven parity classes and with positive atom weights $w_p$. Completeness gives same-parity midpoint closure. It gives a base point $p^*$ such that every closed containing base halfspace has mass at least $1/7$. The trace of an ambient containing halfspace on the zero affine graph contains just such a base halfspace trace, or the whole graph for a constant restriction. At every included base the ambient cap contains its fiber's zero point. It pays at least $(1/2-\varepsilon)w_p$ there, also if the trace is the whole fiber under a pure-base normal. Summing gives $(1/2-\varepsilon)/7$. For $\varepsilon<1/16$ this is strictly greater than $1/16\ge\Gamma_d/8$. If $d\ge2$, the first three binomial terms give $(1+1/d)^d\ge2+(d-1)/(2d)\ge9/4$, so $\Gamma_d\le4/9$. For $\varepsilon\le1/18$ the claimed stronger comparison follows.

statement:
Use the complete thirteen-site base $P$ and widths $w$ of the strict-quota centroid graph obstruction, with total mass one and seven occupied parities. For each $d\ge1$ and any compatible centers $c$ of the specified boxes, the actual centroid of the fiber at index $2$ has mixed raw depth at least $443/5824=1/14+27/5824>\Gamma_d/7$, where $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Its four-site subchain at indices $1,2,3,4$ is a closed base minor of mass $1929/7280<2/7$.

For $c_p=\varepsilon w_p$, $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, the point $0$ in each fiber has exact ordinary raw depth $(1/2-\varepsilon)w_p$. Some actual point $(p^*,0)$ has mixed raw depth at least $(1/2-\varepsilon)/7$. This is strictly greater than $\Gamma_d/8$ when $0<\varepsilon<1/16$, and is at least $\Gamma_d/7$ if $d\ge2$ and $0<\varepsilon\le1/18$.
title: Mixed depth payments on the thirteen-site compatible boxes
